texts.preamble: Babulal Khemchand Nanakvani vs State Of on 30 January, 2013 Author: K.M.Thaker Bench: K.M.Thaker Babulal Khemchand NANAKVANI....Applicant(s)V/SSTATE Of GUJARAT....Respondent(s) R/Cr.Ma/8401/2012 Order
texts.facts: In present petition the petitioner has prayed, inter alia, that:- (a)..... (b) This Hon'ble Court be pleased to quash and [LEAKAGE_MASK] the FIR bearing I C.R. No. 130 of 2012 registered with Mahemdavad Police Station, Dist: Kheda (Annexure-A) and further be pleased to quash and [LEAKAGE_MASK] the proceedings initiate pursuant to FIR in the interest of justice; (c)............. (d)............. Babulal Khemchand Nanakvani vs State Of on 30 January, 2013 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80736730/ 3 1.1 Thus, the petitioner seeks, in present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure that the FIR in respect of alleged offence under Sections 272, 273, 406 and 420 of Indian Penal Code and Sections 50 and 52 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 may be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 1.2 The above quoted relief is prayed for in the background of fact that on 25.2.2012 the complainant i.e. Head Constable, Local Crime Branch Kheda reached along with the other police personnel the factory of the petitioner where they allegedly found oil packed in tins and bottles on which labels of different brands were pasted. The complainant lifted three samples from each tin / bottle and out of 39 bottles 13 bottles were directed to be kept at Police Station and other bottles were sent for analysis to FSL, Ahmedabad. The complainant and team also seized other muddamal lying in the factory. According to the complainant the seized material is found to be not fit for human consumption. Thereafter, the complainant lodged the FIR / complaint which has been registered as C.R.-I No.130 of 2012 2.
texts.arguments: Mr. Parikh, learned advocate for the petitioner has appeared and submitted that in present case the complaint has been filed against the petitioner with regard to the provisions under Indian Penal Code as well as the provisions under Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and the offences which are alleged against the petitioner are the offence punishable under the provisions of the both Acts i.e. Indian Penal Code (Sections 272, 273, 406, 420) as well as Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (Sections 51 and 52). He also submitted that in view of the provision contained under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, police does not have any authority to initiate proceedings and it is only the competent and authorize officer under the Act who can initiate the proceedings by filing complaint before the competent Court of learned Magistrate. He submitted that the proceedings initiated by the police are without jurisdiction and competence and therefore FIR filed against the petitioner deserves to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 3. So as to support his submission learned advocate for the petitioner relied on the decision in case between M/s. Pepsico India Holdings (Pvt.) Ltd vs. State of U.P. (2011 [2] Crimes 250). He relied on the observations made in paragraph Nos. 26 to 28 which read thus:- 26.It He also relied on the decision in case between Shambhu Dayal Agrawal vs. State of Gujarat (2003 [2] GLH 621). 4. In the said decision the Court framed below mentioned issues:- 1) Whether section 22 of the Act would debar even lodging an FIR before the police with respect to the offences punishable under the said Act and the Rules made thereunder ?
